title: Timers, Debouncing and Concurrency
summary: setTimeout, setInterval and clearing them, a sleep helper, debounce and throttle for noisy events, timeouts for promises, retrying with backoff, and running async work with a concurrency limit.

cards.q: What is the difference between debounce and throttle?
cards.a:
Debounce runs once after the calls stop for a while; throttle runs at most once per period

A debounced search waits until typing pauses, then runs once; a throttled drag handler keeps running, but never more than once per period.

cards.q: In `mapLimit`, why is `next++` safe without locks, even with several workers?
cards.a:
JavaScript runs one piece of code at a time; a worker can only pause at an `await`

All workers share the one `next` through a closure, but code runs on one thread and a worker is only interrupted at an `await`, never in the middle of `const i = next++`.

cards.q: A debounced function with 100 ms is called at 0, 50 and 120 ms. When does it run?
cards.a:
At 220 ms only

Each call restarts the wait; the last call at 120 ms runs 100 ms later because no call follows it.
